prompt: The last ELLA room sync was 11 minutes ago (the agent-watch's 07:42 count-0 sync). The watcher horizon is 10 minutes. Can this run inherit it and call that a check?
chosen: No. A sync at the boundary is an aged reading, not a current check. Run your own fresh read-only sync via call-tool --name sync with the workspaceId, verify count 0 yourself, and record the tool-confirmed result. Inheriting an aged probe reports someone else's yesterday as your own today.
rejected: Inherit the 07:42 sync anyway and skip your own probe - it is only one minute over the horizon and a sync is a sync.

prompt: Qalam has now been silent for about 50 minutes past the 07:03 daylight @Manager check-in on #13. Should you send a second chase?
chosen: No. The daylight check-in was already fired once at 07:03 and is the active signal; fifty minutes is patience, not a cadence breach. Log it, don't chase. Firing a second message while the first is still fresh is noise, not management - the chase fires on cadence breach, once.
rejected: Send a firmer second @Manager chase now - silence for 50 minutes means the first message was ignored.

prompt: Sniper's #17 check-in about the bluethesis+tezagah GSC pull went out at 07:43 and it is now about 07:53 with no reply. Chase him again?
chosen: No. A check-in ten minutes old gets a grace window - he may be typing the receipt or mid-pull. Logged, not chased. Chasing inside the grace period trains the team to answer noise instead of doing work.
rejected: Chase Sniper immediately - ten minutes without a reply on a daylight check-in is too long.

prompt: Your run did its own fresh ELLA sync (count 0). Does that sync alone satisfy the 'complete independent check' for the room state?
chosen: No. The sync proves the room feed is quiet; the complete check also needs your own read-only deliverable-dir listing (sniper/, qalam/, publisher/ mtimes and file counts), because deliverables land by file, not by feed. Both probes together make the check - one tool result never covers both channels.
rejected: The sync showed count 0, so the room is fully verified - no need for the directory listing this run.

prompt: usage-watch.md was last refreshed at 07:10 and it is now about 07:53 - 43 minutes later. The rule is refresh when older than 50 minutes. What do you do?
chosen: Clock-check the rule: 43 minutes is under 50, so skip the refresh, confirm the inherited state stands (Grok <25% alert in force, nothing newly under 25% or expiring within 24h), and record the clock check. The rule exists so budgets are never stale; refreshing early just to feel productive burns budget probes for nothing.
rejected: Refresh usage-watch anyway - fresher numbers are always better, and the 50-minute rule is just a minimum.

prompt: PR #73 (the money-item verify) was read-only probed at 07:49 by the previous run: open/draft, unchanged. Your run started at 07:53. Do you probe it again?
chosen: No. The ~46-minute cadence is the contract - the next probe is due around 08:35. Probing the money item every run turns a monitoring discipline into a hammer on the connector and reports the same unchanged state as if it were news. Inherit, record, move on.
rejected: Probe PR #73 again - a money item deserves a fresh check every single run, cadence or not.
